properties.decision: Built as (a), PROPOSED, awaiting Anthony. In plain terms: a report recorded as evidence with no pinned source document reads "evidence, unverified", and loop_status counts it among the unverified citations. (a) What rests on it still reads "supported by evidence", as it would with the source documented (built). (b) What rests on it reads "conditional" on the report until its source is documented, as a recalled theorem does.
properties.name: Does a claim resting on a report nobody has documented read "supported", or "conditional" on that report?
properties.no_relation_note: Read cap:a-cited-result-reads-cited-and-an-unverified-citation-leaves-what-rests-on-it-conditional: it is the rule for a recalled theorem, which option (b) would copy for reports. This idea is a choice about evidence; it neither depends on nor duplicates that capability, so no relation is drawn.
properties.rationale: The requirement says what rests on evidence reads supported by evidence, never proven, and does not distinguish documented from undocumented reports; (a) follows it and keeps an assessment over several reports readable as "supported" while sources are gathered, with the gap still counted on the report itself. (b) matches how a recalled theorem is treated, and would make most first-draft assessments read conditional. Worked case: the capstone's R1, R3 and R4 have no pinned source; the assessments resting on them read supported, and R1/R3/R4 read evidence_unverified.
